note: Only ublituximab (ex-vivo CLL ADCC; GENUINE phase 3) and epcoritamab (monkey, patient CLL PBMC/PDX; EPCORE CLL-1) have CLL model-to-patient comparisons; veltuzumab and MT-3724 have no CLL-specific model source found.
label: CLL/SLL (CD20 depleters)

engagement.population: Unselected (relapsed/refractory CLL/SLL; GENUINE limited to del(17p)/del(11q)/TP53)
engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level (PubMed 18302712). EMAB-6 is the development name of ublituximab (LFB-R603/TG-1101); identity read from the LFB-R603 MeSH supplementary concept, not from the paper.
engagement.model: Primary CLL cells from patients, ex-vivo ADCC/CDC vs rituximab
engagement.note: EMAB-6 (ublituximab) gave more FcγRIIIA-dependent ADCC against patient CLL cells than rituximab; ADCC has no measured counterpart in dosed patients.
engagement.short: Higher ADCC on CLL cells, no human readout
engagement.quote: It induced a higher in vitro antibody-dependent cellular cytotoxicity against CLL cells and a higher FcgammaRIIIA-mediated interleukin-2 production by FcgammaRIIIA(+) Jurkat cells in the presence of CLL cells
engagement.judgement: The model's readout is ex-vivo ADCC; trials reported responses but no ADCC or effector-function readout I could find, so engagement stays untested.

engagement.population: Unselected (relapsed/refractory CLL/SLL; GENUINE limited to del(17p)/del(11q)/TP53)
engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level; model_filed inferred from 'Non-clinical safety studies were performed in cynomolgus monkeys' supporting the FIH trial.
engagement.model: Cynomolgus monkey (B-cell depletion, cytokines, SC vs IV)
engagement.note: Epcoritamab gave profound, long-lasting B-cell depletion in blood and lymphoid organs of cynomolgus monkeys, SC as well as IV.
engagement.quote: In cynomolgus monkeys, DuoBody-CD3xCD20 demonstrated profound and long-lasting B-cell depletion from peripheral blood and lymphoid organs, which was comparable after subcutaneous and intravenous administration.
engagement.judgement: Opening entry; the monkey work precedes the CLL trial (NCT04623541, started 2020-11-25).

engagement.population: Unselected (relapsed/refractory CLL/SLL; GENUINE limited to del(17p)/del(11q)/TP53)
engagement.model: Patient CLL PBMC co-culture and CLL patient-derived xenograft
engagement.note: Epcoritamab expanded and activated autologous T cells in every patient CLL sample ex vivo; T-cell activation in dosed CLL patients not reported in an admissible source.
engagement.quote: Epcoritamab induced significant T-cell expansion, activation, and differentiation into Th1 and effector memory cells in all patient samples.
engagement.judgement: The CLL trial abstract reports IL-6 for CRS, not T-cell expansion, so the readout has no patient comparison yet.

engagement.magnitude_basis: B-cell depletion in monkey blood vs undetectable blood MRD in CLL responders
engagement.population: Unselected (relapsed/refractory CLL/SLL; GENUINE limited to del(17p)/del(11q)/TP53)
engagement.confidence_note: Conference abstract (Blood supplement, DOI verified by scrape); no peer-reviewed paper on the R/R CLL cohort and no registry results for NCT04623541 (first posted 2020-11-10).
engagement.model: Cynomolgus monkey (B-cell depletion, cytokines, SC vs IV)
engagement.note: In R/R CLL, 9 of 12 MRD-evaluable responders had undetectable blood MRD at 10^-4 on epcoritamab 48 mg SC.
engagement.short: Blood CLL cells cleared in most responders
engagement.quote: Among 12 responders evaluable for minimal residual disease (MRD) by next-generation sequencing in peripheral blood, 9 (75%) had undetectable MRD (uMRD) at the standard 10−4 cutoff
engagement.reason: Blood B-cell clearance reproduced in CLL
engagement.judgement: Judgement call: blood MRD of the CD20+ CLL clone stands in for the monkey's peripheral B-cell depletion; paired by me, the abstract does not cite the monkey data.

engagement.note: Low SC or IP veltuzumab depleted circulating and sessile B cells in normal cynomolgus monkeys and controlled human lymphoma xenografts.
engagement.short: Low doses deplete monkey B cells
engagement.quote: Studies of intraperitoneal and subcutaneous doses in mouse models of human lymphoma and in normal cynomolgus monkeys disclosed that low doses of veltuzumab control tumor growth or deplete circulating or sessile B cells.
engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level; first public 2008-10-21 (epub), used as proxy for first use. Full text not retrieved.
engagement.judgement: Opening entry for the veltuzumab track, a class member the draft had no model for.
engagement.model: Cynomolgus monkey B-cell depletion and human lymphoma xenografts dosed with low SC/IP veltuzumab

engagement.magnitude_basis: B-cell depletion in monkey blood vs fall in CLL lymphocytosis after low-dose SC veltuzumab
engagement.note: In 21 CLL patients on low-dose SC veltuzumab, lymphocytosis fell in all, by more than half in 12.
engagement.short: Lymphocytosis fell in every CLL patient
engagement.quote: Lymphocytosis decreased in all patients (maximum decrease, 5-91%), with 12 patients obtaining >50% decreases.
engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level; trial taken as NCT00546793 (SC veltuzumab in NHL and CLL, first posted 2007-10-19), not stated in the abstract.
engagement.reason: Low-dose depletion reproduced in CLL blood
engagement.judgement: Paired by me: fall in circulating CLL cells stands in for the monkey's circulating B-cell depletion, the same readout the draft's epcoritamab-cyno track uses.
engagement.model: Cynomolgus monkey B-cell depletion and human lymphoma xenografts dosed with low SC/IP veltuzumab

dose.population: Unselected (relapsed/refractory CLL/SLL; GENUINE limited to del(17p)/del(11q)/TP53)
dose.confidence_note: Abstract-level. EMAB-6 is the development name of ublituximab (LFB-R603/TG-1101); identity read from the LFB-R603 MeSH supplementary concept, not from the paper.
dose.model: Primary CLL cells from patients, ex-vivo ADCC/CDC vs rituximab
dose.note: The model argued the ADCC gain was largest at low antibody doses, suggesting lower doses; no exposure or regimen target was stated.
dose.quote: Comparative studies between CLL and lymphoma cells coated with EMAB-6 or rituximab indicated that the difference of efficacy was more pronounced at low doses and when target cells expressed fewer CD20 molecules.
dose.reason: No human dose or exposure stated
dose.judgement: Qualitative 'lower doses possible' is not a checkable exposure target; ublituximab was in fact given at 900 mg in CLL.

dose.population: Unselected (relapsed/refractory CLL/SLL; GENUINE limited to del(17p)/del(11q)/TP53)
dose.confidence_note: Abstract-level; the FDA epcoritamab review (DLBCL) was not read for a MABEL/NOAEL statement.
dose.model: Cynomolgus monkey (B-cell depletion, cytokines, SC vs IV)
dose.note: Monkey data supported SC dosing with comparable bioavailability; the abstract states no human exposure target or margin, and the 48 mg dose came from NHL patients.
dose.short: SC route supported, no dose target
dose.quote: Peak plasma levels of DuoBody-CD3xCD20 were lower and delayed after subcutaneous administration, which was associated with a reduction in plasma cytokine levels compared to intravenous administration, while bioavailability was comparable.
dose.judgement: Route and bioavailability are not an exposure, occupancy or margin target, so dose stays untested; the CLL regimen (48 mg) was taken from EPCORE NHL-1.

dose.note: The models said only that low doses suffice; no human dose, exposure target or margin. Kalaycio 2016 found no exposure-response across 80-320 mg SC.
dose.short: Low dose claimed, no human target
dose.quote: Low- and high-dose veltuzumab were significantly more effective in vivo than rituximab in 3 lymphoma models.
dose.confidence_note: Abstract-level; full text may state monkey doses but no human exposure target was found.
dose.judgement: 'Low doses work' is qualitative; no human exposure, regimen or margin to score, so untested.
dose.model: Cynomolgus monkey B-cell depletion and human lymphoma xenografts dosed with low SC/IP veltuzumab

efficacy.population: Unselected (relapsed/refractory CLL/SLL; GENUINE limited to del(17p)/del(11q)/TP53)
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level. EMAB-6 is the development name of ublituximab (LFB-R603/TG-1101); identity read from the LFB-R603 MeSH supplementary concept, not from the paper.
efficacy.model: Primary CLL cells from patients, ex-vivo ADCC/CDC vs rituximab
efficacy.note: Ex-vivo patient CLL cells predicted ublituximab would be a promising CLL drug, especially where CD20 is low.
efficacy.quote: Thus, EMAB-6 mAb represents a promising drug candidate for the treatment of CLL by inducing a strong cytotoxicity against tumour cells that express low CD20 levels.
efficacy.judgement: Opening entry for the ublituximab track.

efficacy.magnitude_basis: ex-vivo ADCC gain vs added overall response rate (83% vs 65%)
efficacy.population: Unselected (relapsed/refractory CLL/SLL; GENUINE limited to del(17p)/del(11q)/TP53)
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level (PubMed 33631112, epub 2021-02-22); registry results posted 2022-05-20. Topline was presented at ASCO 2017, not used for dating.
efficacy.model: Primary CLL cells from patients, ex-vivo ADCC/CDC vs rituximab
efficacy.note: GENUINE: adding ublituximab to ibrutinib raised IRC-assessed ORR from 65% to 83% (p=0.020) in high-risk R/R CLL.
efficacy.quote: After a median follow-up of 41·6 months (IQR 36·7-47·3), the overall response rate was 53 (83%) of 64 patients in the ublituximab plus ibrutinib group and 40 (65%) of 62 patients in the ibrutinib group (p=0·020).

patient_trials.quote: Combination therapy resulted in an overall response rate (ORR) of 88% at 6 months.
The overall response rate for evaluable patients (n = 31) was 45% (13% complete responses, 32% partial responses).

efficacy.judgement: Judgement call: GENUINE isolates ublituximab's contribution, so it tests the model's class prediction; the model's sharper claim (superior to rituximab) was never tested head to head in CLL. Primary endpoint was amended from co-primary PFS+ORR to ORR alone. UNITY-CLL (ublituximab+umbralisib vs obinutuzumab+chlorambucil) cannot isolate ublituximab and is not scored.

efficacy.population: Unselected (relapsed/refractory CLL/SLL; GENUINE limited to del(17p)/del(11q)/TP53)
efficacy.model: Patient CLL PBMC co-culture and CLL patient-derived xenograft
efficacy.note: Epcoritamab killed patient CLL cells ex vivo regardless of CD20 level, including samples progressing on BTKi, and cut blood and spleen burden in CLL PDX mice.
efficacy.quote: Cytotoxic activity was independent of CD20 expression on CLL cells and observed in samples from patients whose condition progressed while receiving BTKi.
efficacy.judgement: Opening entry. Possible retrodiction: early EPCORE CLL-1 escalation data were public at ASH 2022 (not verified); I scored it as prospective because the experiments used no trial data.

efficacy.magnitude_basis: ex-vivo killing of BTKi-exposed CLL cells vs ORR in BTKi-exposed R/R CLL
efficacy.population: Unselected (relapsed/refractory CLL/SLL; GENUINE limited to del(17p)/del(11q)/TP53)
efficacy.confidence_note: Conference abstract (Blood supplement, DOI verified by scrape); no peer-reviewed paper on the R/R CLL cohort and no registry results for NCT04623541 (first posted 2020-11-10). Single-arm, no prespecified bar in the abstract.
efficacy.model: Patient CLL PBMC co-culture and CLL patient-derived xenograft
efficacy.note: EPCORE CLL-1 expansion: ORR 61%, CR 39% in R/R CLL, all BTKi-exposed and 85% also BCL2i-exposed.
efficacy.quote: In EXP, ORR was 61% and CR rate was 39%.
efficacy.judgement: Judgement call: a single-arm 61% ORR in BTKi/BCL2i-exposed CLL is read as the class working; scored on a conference abstract (low confidence). The Richter transformation cohort (Lancet Haematol 2026, ORR 47.6%, missed its 50% alternative) is DLBCL histology and not scored in this CLL/SLL context.

patient_trials.quote: By NCI-WG criteria, two patients achieved partial responses (10%).

efficacy.note: Xenograft tumour control; the only CLL trial was a phase I with a safety primary endpoint (2/21 partial responses), no efficacy readout.
efficacy.short: Xenograft control; CLL phase I only
efficacy.quote: These findings are consistent with activity in patients with non-Hodgkin lymphoma given low intravenous or subcutaneous doses of veltuzumab.
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level. Xenografts were lymphoma lines, not CLL.
efficacy.reason: Only a safety-primary phase I in CLL
efficacy.judgement: A 10% partial-response rate in a safety-primary phase I is neither a match nor a miss on a primary efficacy endpoint.
efficacy.model: Cynomolgus monkey B-cell depletion and human lymphoma xenografts dosed with low SC/IP veltuzumab

safety.population: Unselected (relapsed/refractory CLL/SLL; GENUINE limited to del(17p)/del(11q)/TP53)
safety.confidence_note: Abstract-level; the full monkey cytokine data and any clinical-sign findings were not read.
safety.model: Cynomolgus monkey (B-cell depletion, cytokines, SC vs IV)
safety.note: Monkeys released plasma cytokines after epcoritamab, less after SC than IV dosing.
safety.quote: Peak plasma levels of DuoBody-CD3xCD20 were lower and delayed after subcutaneous administration, which was associated with a reduction in plasma cytokine levels compared to intravenous administration, while bioavailability was comparable.
safety.judgement: Opening entry: the stated harm is cytokine release, which monkeys can show.

safety.magnitude_basis: plasma cytokines in monkeys vs CRS incidence in CLL patients
safety.population: Unselected (relapsed/refractory CLL/SLL; GENUINE limited to del(17p)/del(11q)/TP53)
safety.confidence_note: Conference abstract (Blood supplement, DOI verified by scrape); no peer-reviewed paper on the R/R CLL cohort and no registry results for NCT04623541 (first posted 2020-11-10).
safety.model: Cynomolgus monkey (B-cell depletion, cytokines, SC vs IV)
safety.note: CRS occurred in 96% of R/R CLL patients (17% grade 3), mainly after the first full dose; an extra step-up dose cut severity.
safety.quote: The most frequent nonhematologic tx-emergent AEs (TEAEs) in EXP were CRS (96%), diarrhea (48%), peripheral edema (48%), fatigue (43%), and injection-site reaction (43%).
safety.reason: Predicted cytokine release appeared as CRS
safety.judgement: Judgement call: the monkey's cytokine signal counts as a stated CRS prediction that held; the model did not state incidence or grade, so direction only. CRS is a CD3-engager platform harm, so it carries modality antibody.
